# Phase 1.2: Provider Config + Encryption + Budget Enforcement - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-05-21
**Status:** Ready for planning
**Mode:** Auto-generated by autonomous run (smart-discuss recommendations applied per workflow.smart_discuss)

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Land the per-subdomain provider config layer + AES-256-GCM key encryption + atomic budget enforcement. Workspace admins can connect any of 6 provider kinds (OpenAI / Anthropic / Google Gemini / Azure OpenAI / Ollama / OpenAI-compatible base URL) with encrypted API keys, edit them without re-entering, remove them, and press "Test connection" to verify reachability. Every chargeable call goes through a pre-check that atomically reserves estimated cost — exceeding the cap throws `BudgetExceededError` before the provider is called. Race-free under 100 concurrent invocations.

In scope:
- `ai_providers` Mongoose model (Phase 1.1 has no models; this is the first one)
- `ai_models` Mongoose model (model registry per provider)
- `ai_budgets` Mongoose model (monthly USD caps per workspace/team/user/agent)
- Provider CRUD: tRPC + GraphQL surface for `aiProvidersAdd/Edit/Remove/Test/List`
- Model listing: `aiModels(providerId)` lists capabilities, context window, cost (admins can override)
- AES-256-GCM encryption: `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` from Phase 1.1 wired into resolver boundary (Provider Mongoose schema has ONLY `encryptedApiKey`, never raw `apiKey`)
- Budget atomic reserve / reconcile / release via Redis token bucket (DECISION LOCKED — see D-02)
- `ERXES_SECRET` rotation: versioned envelope already shipped Phase 1.1; this phase ships the rotation script and multi-version decrypt fallback (DECISION LOCKED — see D-03)
- `Test connection` calls the provider with the decrypted key, returns latency + model list, never returns the key
- Concrete provider adapters (HTTP-level): OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible — all implementing `ILLMProvider` from Phase 1.1, just `listModels()` + a thin smoke-test wrapper. `chat()` and `embed()` implementations defer to Phase 1.3.
- CI grep gate: no Mongoose schema field named `apiKey` (only `encryptedApiKey`) — P13 mitigation
- Integration test: 100 concurrent `Promise.all([invoke()] × 100)` against a $5 cap → spend ≤ $5

Out of scope (deferred):
- `trpc.ai.llm.chat`/`embed` implementations — Phase 1.3
- Provider-native structured output (Zod → JSON Schema) — Phase 1.3
- Audit log `ai_invocations` writes — Phase 1.3
- Settings UI rendering of Providers / Models / Budgets pages — Phase 1.4
- Cost dashboard time-series — Phase 1.4
- Tool registry — Phase 2.1
- Agent loop — Phase 2.2

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Module Layout (continues Phase 1.1)
- **D-01:** Provider/Model/Budget Mongoose schemas live under `backend/plugins/ai_api/src/models/definitions/{providers,models,budgets}.ts`. Model classes that wrap them: `backend/plugins/ai_api/src/models/{Providers,Models,Budgets}.ts`. `connectionResolvers.ts` exports `IModels { AiProviders, AiModels, AiBudgets }` and `loadClasses` instantiates them per subdomain via `createGenerateModels<IModels>(loadClasses)` (mirrors `sales_api/src/connectionResolvers.ts`).
- **D-01b:** Module folders that ship in Phase 1.2 under `backend/plugins/ai_api/src/modules/`: `providers/`, `models/`, `budgets/`. Each has `mutations.ts`, `queries.ts`, `service.ts`, `index.ts`. Apollo resolver/typedef references move from `src/apollo/resolvers/{queries,mutations}.ts` into per-module files following the pattern `backend/plugins/sales_api/src/modules/sales/` uses.
- **D-01c:** Provider adapters land at `backend/erxes-api-shared/src/ai/providers/{openai,anthropic,google,azure,ollama}.ts`. Each implements `ILLMProvider` from `providers/base.ts` (shipped Phase 1.1). `providers/index.ts` exports a registry: `resolveProvider(kind, config) → ILLMProvider`. Azure shares OpenAI's client with a different baseURL + `deploymentName`. Ollama shares OpenAI's client (OpenAI-compatible). "OpenAI-compatible" is the same path with a custom `baseURL` field.

### Budget Strategy — LOCKED Redis token bucket (PITFALLS §P2 Option A)
- **D-02:** Budget enforcement uses a Redis token bucket per `(subdomain, scope, scopeId, yyyyMM)` keyed `ai:budget:{subdomain}:{scope}:{scopeId}:{yyyyMM}`. The MongoDB `ai_budgets` collection stores the cap definition + alert thresholds; the Redis key stores the actual current-month spend (in cents). Pre-check pattern:
  ```ts
  // modules/budgets/check.ts
  const estimatedCents = estimateCost(model, inputTokens, toolDefsOverheadTokens);
  const newSpend = await redis.incrby(key, estimatedCents);
  if (newSpend > capCents) {
    await redis.decrby(key, estimatedCents);  // rollback reservation
    throw new BudgetExceededError({ scope, scopeId, currentSpend: newSpend - estimatedCents, cap: capCents });
  }
  // ... make the LLM call (Phase 1.3) ...
  // reconcile actual vs estimated after provider returns
  const diff = actualCents - estimatedCents;
  if (diff !== 0) await redis.incrby(key, diff);  // can be negative
  await redis.expire(key, secondsToEndOfMonth);
  ```
  MongoDB `ai_budgets.currentMonthSpend` is reconciled nightly from `ai_invocations` aggregate (Phase 1.3 owns the writer). Audit log is the source of truth for billing.
- **D-02b:** `BudgetExceededError` extends a base `AIError` class and carries `{ scope, scopeId, currentSpend, cap, suggestionUrl }` so the UI can deep-link to `/settings/ai/budgets`.
- **D-02c:** Alert thresholds (BUDG-05) are written into `ai_budgets.alertThresholds[]` (Phase 1.2 ships storage + admin write). The trigger emission to the automation engine (`ai:budgetExceeded`) is Phase 3.1 — Phase 1.2 only stores the configuration and emits a Redis pubsub event `ai:budget:threshold:{subdomain}:{scope}:{scopeId}` on crossing for the audit log to listen to later.

### ERXES_SECRET Rotation — LOCKED Policy A (versioned envelope + script)
- **D-03:** `ERXES_SECRET` becomes a comma-separated versioned secret list: `ERXES_SECRET=v2:hex...,v1:hex...` (newest first). `decryptSecret(ciphertext, subdomain)` parses the envelope's `version`, looks up the matching key, validates auth tag. The encryption envelope already shipped Phase 1.1: `{ version: 1, iv, ciphertext, authTag }` (base64-joined).
- **D-03b:** `validateErxesSecret()` in `ai_api/src/main.ts` (Phase 1.1) is extended to parse the comma-separated list. Each entry must be `v\d+:<32 hex bytes>`. Backwards compat: a bare 32-hex string is treated as `v1:<hex>` automatically.
- **D-03c:** Rotation script at `scripts/ai/rotate-secret.ts`:
  - Reads every `ai_providers` doc across all subdomains
  - Decrypts `encryptedApiKey` with the OLDEST version that succeeds
  - Re-encrypts with the NEWEST version
  - Writes back to MongoDB
  - Idempotent: re-running is safe (if already v2-encrypted, skips)
  - Dry-run mode: `pnpm tsx scripts/ai/rotate-secret.ts --dry-run`
- **D-03d:** Document rotation procedure in `CLAUDE.md` Operations section (Phase 3.2 owns the CLAUDE.md update; Phase 1.2 ships a `scripts/ai/README.md` with the procedure for now).

### Google SDK — LOCKED Modern `@google/genai`
- **D-04:** Replace original CONTEXT D-13's `@google/generative-ai@0.24.1` with **`@google/genai@^1.x` (latest stable as of plan-phase)**. Justification: Phase 1.1's D-09 ADDENDUM aligned Docker base to `node:22-alpine3.22`, lifting the `Node 20+` constraint that originally forced the legacy SDK. The modern SDK has the newer API surface (system instructions, structured output, streaming) and active maintenance. Plan-phase researcher MUST verify exact version + install command via Context7 or `npm view @google/genai version` at plan time and pin in `package.json`.
- **D-04b:** `STACK.md` "do not use `@google/genai`" rationale is OBSOLETE. Update the doc in a planning revision (low priority — surface in Phase 1.2 SUMMARY).

### Provider Adapters — Phase 1.2 ships scaffolding + listModels + Test Connection
- **D-05:** Each `ILLMProvider` implementation in Phase 1.2 ships:
  - `listModels(): Promise<ProviderModel[]>` — calls the provider's models endpoint, returns `{ modelId, capabilities, contextWindow }[]`
  - `testConnection(): Promise<{ ok: boolean, latencyMs: number, modelsAvailable: number, errorCode?: string }>` — returns connection health summary (no key in response per P1)

  - `embed(req): Promise<EmbedResponse>` — **STUB** that throws `NotYetImplementedError('Phase 1.3 wires real embed')`
- **D-05b:** Provider SDK pins (verify exact at plan-phase time via Context7):
  - `openai@^6.x` (latest stable)
  - `@anthropic-ai/sdk@^0.x.latest`
  - `@google/genai@^1.x` (per D-04 — NOT @google/generative-ai)
  - Azure shares `openai` SDK with `AzureOpenAI` export
  - Ollama uses raw `fetch` (OpenAI-compatible JSON shape; no SDK needed)
  - OpenAI-compatible uses raw `fetch` with custom `baseURL`
- **D-05c:** Provider adapters live in `erxes-api-shared/src/ai/providers/` (alongside `base.ts` from Phase 1.1). The registry `providers/index.ts` keys on `ProviderKind` discriminator from `types.ts`.

### Encryption-at-Resolver-Boundary (P13 mitigation)
- **D-06:** The `aiProvidersAdd` and `aiProvidersEdit` resolvers encrypt the `apiKey` field BEFORE invoking the Mongoose model. The Mongoose schema has ONLY `encryptedApiKey: { type: String, required: true }` — there is NO `apiKey` field in the schema. The resolver extracts `apiKey` from `doc`, encrypts it via `encryptSecret(apiKey, subdomain)` from `erxes-api-shared/ai/encryption`, deletes the plaintext from the local `doc` variable, then passes to `models.AiProviders.create({ ...doc, encryptedApiKey })`.
- **D-06b:** GraphQL `AiProvider` type has `hasApiKey: Boolean!` (computed: `encryptedApiKey != null`) but NO field that exposes the encrypted or decrypted value. `aiProvidersTest` resolver returns `{ ok, latencyMs, modelsAvailable: [...] }` — never echoes any portion of the key.
- **D-06c:** Edit-without-rotate mode: when `aiProvidersEdit` is called with `doc.apiKey == null` (UI sends empty when admin doesn't touch the field), the existing `encryptedApiKey` is preserved unchanged. The resolver detects this via the input being `undefined` (not `''`). When admin types a new key, full re-encrypt with new IV.
- **D-06d:** CI grep gate (queued for Phase 1.2): `git grep -l 'apiKey' backend/plugins/ai_api/src/models/` returns 0. Add the gate to CI workflow.

### Test Connection Rate Limiting (security mistake mitigation)
- **D-07:** `aiProvidersTest` is rate-limited per admin user: 10 calls/hour via Redis token bucket `ai:test:{subdomain}:{userId}:{yyyy-MM-dd-HH}`. Prevents abuse as an "is this key valid?" oracle. Every call writes to a `ai_provider_test_audit` collection (Phase 1.2 ships the model; tested but not surfaced in UI until Phase 1.4).

### Budget Race Acceptance Gate (BUDG-04)
- **D-08:** Integration test at `backend/plugins/ai_api/src/__tests__/budget-race.test.ts`:
  - Seed a workspace budget with `monthlyUsdCap: 5.00` (500 cents) for a test scope
  - Spawn 100 simultaneous `Promise.all` invocations of the budget pre-check via `modules/budgets/check.ts` (mock the LLM call to return a fixed `actualCents = 1`)
  - Assert: `final Redis key value <= 500` AND number of BudgetExceededError throws + number of successes = 100
  - Run with `pnpm nx test ai_api -- budget-race.test.ts`
  - Uses a real Redis (testcontainers or ioredis-mock — pick at plan time; test container preferred for fidelity per integration test honesty)

### Provider Adapter Test Strategy
- **D-09:** Unit tests per adapter (mock fetch / mock SDK):
  - OpenAI: `listModels()` returns expected shape from mocked `/v1/models` response; `testConnection()` succeeds; thrown errors don't include the API key (P1 acceptance gate)
  - Anthropic: same — verify Anthropic's specific error shape (`Authentication`/`PermissionDenied`/`NotFound`) is caught and sanitized
  - Google: same for `@google/genai`
  - Azure: same with `deploymentName` URL construction
  - Ollama: same against raw fetch (OpenAI-compatible)
- **D-09b:** Integration test: with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set in env (gated `it.skip(!process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY)`), actually call `listModels()` and `testConnection()` against the real OpenAI endpoint. Verify > 5 models returned. This is the proof the smoke path works against real infra.

### Claude's Discretion
- Exact Mongoose schema timestamps vs explicit `createdAt`/`updatedAt`/`createdBy` — copy the convention from `backend/plugins/sales_api/src/models/definitions/deals.ts` exactly.
- Whether the rotation script uses streaming cursor or `find().exec()` for the rewrite loop — planner can choose based on expected provider count (most workspaces have <50 providers, `find()` is fine; if a streaming cursor is trivial, use it).
- Test container vs `ioredis-mock` for budget-race test — testcontainers preferred for fidelity, but adds a Docker dependency. Planner can pick `ioredis-mock` if Docker-in-CI is a concern; surface tradeoff in SUMMARY.
- Whether to ship a `aiProvidersImport` GraphQL mutation that lets admins paste a `.env` block (multiple keys at once) — defer to Phase 1.4 unless trivial.

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### Reusable Assets (from Phase 1.1)
- **`encryptSecret(plaintext, subdomain)` / `decryptSecret(ciphertext, subdomain)`** at `backend/erxes-api-shared/src/ai/encryption.ts` — production-tested versioned envelope. Phase 1.2 extends to multi-version `ERXES_SECRET` parsing.
- **`redactKey()` regex** at `backend/erxes-api-shared/src/ai/redaction.ts` — used in provider adapter error chains
- **`COST_TABLE` + `DRIFT_MULTIPLIER`** at `backend/erxes-api-shared/src/ai/tokens.ts` — used by budget pre-check estimator
- **`createAIClient` + `AINotEnabledError`** — irrelevant in 1.2 (this code lives INSIDE ai_api so it never hits the shim)
- **`redis` client** at `backend/erxes-api-shared/src/utils/redis.ts` — for the budget token bucket
- **`isEnabled(name)` from `service-discovery.ts`** — irrelevant in 1.2

### Established Patterns
- **Mongoose model with class wrapper**: schema in `models/definitions/`, class in `models/`. The class has `static createX`, `static updateX`, etc. — business logic goes in the class methods, not in resolvers. Resolvers are thin wrappers.
- **Module folder pattern**: `src/modules/{feature}/{mutations,queries,service,types}.ts` — keeps the apollo/typeDefs.ts file small. Resolvers in `apollo/resolvers/{queries,mutations}.ts` re-export from each module.
- **tRPC router per module**: `src/trpc/routers/{feature}.ts` exports a router, `init-trpc.ts` mergers them into `appRouter`.
- **Subdomain context**: `subdomain` is the only positional argument passed to `generateModels` and to `encryptSecret` — every collection access is automatically tenant-scoped via Mongoose connection.

### Integration Points
- **Apollo Federation** — `AiProvider @key(fields: "_id")` is a federated type. Phase 1.2's `__resolveReference` is trivial (look up by _id). Federation gateway will compose this with `User` (for `createdBy: User`).
- **Gateway pubsub** — Phase 1.2 emits `ai:budget:threshold:{subdomain}:{scope}:{scopeId}` on Redis pubsub when alert thresholds are crossed. Phase 1.3's audit log subscribes; Phase 3.1 wires the automation trigger.
- **`ai_api` GraphQL surface** — Phase 1.1 has `_aiPing`/`_aiNoop` placeholders. Phase 1.2 replaces these with real `aiProviders`, `aiProvider`, `aiModels`, `aiBudgets`, `aiProvidersAdd/Edit/Remove/Test`, `aiBudgetsSet`, etc.

</code_context>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- Budget pre-check must include tool definition overhead (P8 mitigation). The estimator: `userInputTokens + toolOverheadTokens + systemPromptTokens + historyTokens`. Phase 1.2 ships this as a function in `modules/budgets/estimate.ts`; Phase 2.1 wires `toolOverheadTokens` when tools are passed.
- `BudgetExceededError` includes a `suggestionUrl: '/settings/ai/budgets?scope=workspace&scopeId=<id>'` so the UI can deep-link with the over-budget scope pre-selected.
- Rotation script supports `--dry-run`, `--subdomain <slug>` (limit to one tenant), and `--verbose` flags. Logs which doc IDs were re-encrypted, never logs ciphertext.
- Test Connection rate limiter logs each test attempt to `ai_provider_test_audit` (collection has `subdomain`, `userId`, `providerId`, `attemptedAt`, `succeeded`, `latencyMs`, `errorCode?`). 30-day TTL.
- The Azure provider's `deploymentName` field is stored as part of the encrypted-or-clear config blob alongside the API key — clarify schema: `config: { deploymentName, apiVersion }` is plaintext; only the API key is encrypted.

</specifics>
